title: Cocartesian sections realize enhanced limits of transport diagrams
statement: Let $C$ be a small ordinary category, let $D$ be a strict functor from $C$ to small quasicategories, and let $q:Q\to N(C)$ be a cocartesian fibration of quasicategories, with $Q$ in the containing universe, together with a strict presentation $\varphi:G_C(D)\to Q$ of $q$ by $D$ [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration]. Then evaluation on fibres, with the transport equivalences, exhibits $\Gamma_{\mathrm{cocart}}(N(C),Q)$ as the enhanced limit $\operatorname{holim}_{N(C)}D$ of the diagram $D:N(C)\to\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, with limits and equivalences understood as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. In particular it is equivalent to the enhanced category of coherent compatible systems $x_c\in D(c)$ with equivalences $D(f)(x_c)\simeq x_d$ for every arrow $f:c\to d$, together with the compatibility data for every simplex of $N(C)$; the equivalence at $f$ attached to a cocartesian section $s$ compares the cocartesian edge $s(f)$ with the cocartesian edge $\varphi(f,s_0x_c)$, where $x_c\in D(c)$ corresponds to $s(c)$. Morphisms are coherent transformations of such systems and need not be equivalences. This is an equivalence of quasicategories on all mapping spaces and higher simplices, retaining the evaluations and transport equivalences. It is natural in two senses. For a functor $u:C'\to C$ of small categories, $\varphi$ pulls back to a strict presentation of $N(u)^*Q$ by $Du$, and restriction of cocartesian sections corresponds to restriction of the limit along $N(u)$. For a strict natural transformation $\eta:D\to D'$, a second such datum $(Q',\varphi')$ over $N(C)$ and a map $g:Q\to Q'$ over $N(C)$ preserving cocartesian edges with $g\varphi=\varphi'\circ G_C(\eta)$, where $G_C(\eta)(\sigma,\tau)=(\sigma,\eta_{\sigma(0)}\tau)$, the map of cocartesian sections induced by $g$ corresponds to the map of limits induced by $\eta$.

source.place: Proposition 7.4.4.1 (Tag 05RX) and Corollary 7.4.4.2 (Tag 02TK), limits as cocartesian sections of a cocartesian fibration with covariant transport representation (Definition 5.6.5.1, Tag 028V); comparison of strict diagrams with transport representations, Subsection 5.6.4 (Tag 0279). The strict presentation is a quasi-equivalence over each simplex in the sense of Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Definition 3.2.2.6 and Proposition 3.2.2.7 (printed pp. 180-181), dualized. WANTED: archived Kerodon and HTT.

proof.text: Put $S=N(C)$. Apply [lem-cbc-strict-presentation-transport-representation] to $D,q,\varphi$. It supplies the coherent equivalence $\alpha:D\simeq\operatorname{St}_S(q)$, with components $\varphi_c$ and represented lifts $\varphi(f,s_0x)$. Write $\beta$ for its inverse. The marked comparison applies to $G_C(D)$ without an inner-fibration hypothesis: it extends the given marked presentation along the map to the relative nerve and identifies the resulting coherent transport with $D$.

source.place: Opening compactification choice; strict presentation to coherent transport (HTT §§3.2.2 and 3.2.5; Kerodon 0279 and 028V).

proof.text: Choose a universe $\mathcal U$ in which $S,Q$ and every $D(c)$ are small, and form $\mathrm{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$ and $\operatorname{coCart}_{\mathcal U}(S)$ in a further containing universe. By [lem-cbc-cocartesian-section-currying], $L=\Gamma_{\mathrm{cocart}}(S,Q)$ is a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory (its simplices are families of maps between $\mathcal U$-small simplicial sets) and its evaluation $e:S\times L\to Q$ is a cocartesian map. Straightening [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] takes $e$ to a coherent transformation $\Delta_S L\to\operatorname{St}_S(q)$, because the source product is classified by $\Delta_S L$. Compose with $\beta$ to obtain a cone $\lambda:\Delta_S L\to D$. Its component at $c$ evaluates a section at $c$ and uses the inverse of $\varphi_c$. Thus the candidate limiting cone is the one in the statement, rather than an unspecified equivalence of its apex.

source.place: Opening compactification choice; section evaluation, straightening, and the coherent cone definition.

proof.text:
For every $\mathcal U$-small testing quasicategory $A$, the coherent-nerve mapping-space comparison [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], the section currying theorem [lem-cbc-cocartesian-section-currying], and the fully faithful straightening equivalence [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Cat}_\infty}(A,L)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(A,L)^\simeq\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{coCart}(S)}(S\times A,Q)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathrm{Cat}_\infty)}(\Delta_S A,\operatorname{St}_S(q))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathrm{Cat}_\infty)}(\Delta_S A,D).$$
The last map postcomposes with $\beta$. An $a:A\to L$ is sent to the currying of $e\circ(\mathrm{id}_S\times a)$, hence to $\lambda\circ\Delta_S(a)$ on the entire mapping space, by the evaluation and naturality clauses of the two theorems. This is precisely the cone-induced map, and every displayed comparison is an equivalence of spaces. The limiting-cone criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], applied in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, therefore proves that $\lambda$ is a limiting cone. The straightening theorem is applied with the fixed $\mathcal U$ just chosen: $S,Q,S\times A$ are $\mathcal U$-small, and $L$ is $\mathcal U$-small by the section formula. All mapping spaces are formed in a larger universe. Enlarging $\mathcal U$ first accommodates any given $Q$ in the containing universe, so no requirement that $Q$ be small in the original fibre universe is added. No completeness, presentability, or Kan-fibre hypothesis is used.

source.place: Opening compactification choice; mapping-space proof of the section-limit theorem, compare Kerodon 05RX/02TK, using existing straightening and cone calculus.

proof.text: The coherent cone $\lambda$ retains the required compatible systems. Its components are fibre evaluations through $\beta_c$, and its edge over $f:c\to d$ is an equivalence $D(f)(x_c)\simeq x_d$: naturality in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ means a natural equivalence between the two evaluation functors. By the transport clause of [lem-cbc-strict-presentation-transport-representation], this is the comparison between $s(f)$ and $\varphi(f,s_0x_c)$, with the chosen fibre equivalences inserted. Its simplices over every string of arrows supply all higher compatibilities. In [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the functor category and coherent cone keep exactly these transformations and higher simplices. By [lem-cbc-cocartesian-section-currying] the category $L$ contains arbitrary transformations between its section objects, not just equivalences. Thus the limit is the stated enhanced category of systems with arbitrary coherent morphisms. The functor-equivalence clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] gives equivalences on every mapping space.

source.place: Opening compactification choice; identify the specific fibre evaluations, transport comparisons, morphisms and higher data.

proof.text: For $u:C'\to C$, the simplex formula [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration] gives a canonical identification $G_{C'}(Du)=N(u)^*G_C(D)$: in degree $n$ both sides are a string $\sigma:[n]\to C'$ and $\tau\in D(u\sigma(0))_n$, and their operators and markings coincide. Hence the pulled-back map $\varphi_u$ preserves marked edges and has fibre map $\varphi_{u(c')}$; it is a strict presentation. The pullback clause of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] and that of [lem-cbc-strict-presentation-transport-representation] identify its transport comparison with the restriction of $\alpha$. For a family of sections $h:S\times A\times\Delta^n\to Q$, restriction is $h\circ(N(u)\times\mathrm{id}_A\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^n})$, paired with the projection into $N(u)^*Q$. The restriction clause of [lem-cbc-cocartesian-section-currying] therefore identifies its cone with $\lambda$ restricted along $N(u)$, in every parameter degree. In the mapping-space calculation of step 3, the square with left side section restriction and right side restriction $\operatorname{Map}(\Delta_S A,D)\to\operatorname{Map}(\Delta_{N(C')} A,Du)$ commutes. The cone criterion [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] characterizes the map of limits by this very square; this proves the pullback naturality clause.

source.place: Opening compactification choice; pullback formula and its explicit square on parameterized section maps.

proof.text: For $(g,\eta)$ as in the statement, let $\alpha',\beta'$ be the corresponding transport comparisons for $q'$. The compatibility clause of [lem-cbc-strict-presentation-transport-representation] turns $g\varphi=\varphi'G_C(\eta)$ into $\operatorname{St}(g)\alpha\simeq\alpha'\eta$, hence $\beta'\operatorname{St}(g)\simeq\eta\beta$. Postcomposition sends a family $h:S\times A\times\Delta^n\to Q$ to $g\circ h$. The postcomposition clause of [lem-cbc-cocartesian-section-currying] says this is the map $g_*:L\to L'$ and commutes with evaluation. Straightening is a functor [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], so the resulting transformation of the rightmost term of step 3 is exactly $t\mapsto\eta\circ t$, using the displayed comparison between $\beta'\operatorname{St}(g)$ and $\eta\beta$. Thus the cone of $g_*$ is coherently $\eta\lambda$, which by the cone criterion [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] is the map of limits induced by $\eta$. For every $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, $g\circ(h\circ(\mathrm{id}_{S\times A}\times\Delta\theta))=(g\circ h)\circ(\mathrm{id}_{S\times A}\times\Delta\theta)$; this degreewise identity, together with the coherent comparison for $\alpha$, verifies the claimed naturality on higher simplices, rather than only on objects.

source.place: Opening compactification choice; explicit represented-map naturality square, including every transformation parameter.
